title: Progressive validation gateway for LTS pinning and rollout fidelity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal:
Implement a Progressive Validation Gateway (PVG) that enforces a series of automated checks before a rollout advances between stages (canary -> ramp -> global) and guarantees compatibility with LTS-pinned clusters. The gateway should be pluggable into our release orchestration so that different release types (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) can reuse the same checks and thresholds.

Background / Motivation:
- Recent rollouts flagged intermittent regressions that were only detected after significant traffic exposure. We need a stronger automated stoplight that combines lightweight smoke sanity, perf regression heuristics, and targeted eval-suite checks keyed to LTS compatibility.
- LTS channels require deterministic guarantees: model serialization compatibility, KV cache warm-up behavior, and quantized kernel fallbacks must meet baseline SLOs.

Success criteria:
- PVG blocks at least 95% of regressions that would have caused >5% error spike in production within first 24h of rollout in synthetic replay tests.
- Integration with Console metrics dashboard: per-stage pass/fail visible and auditable with links to failing test artifacts.
- Can be configured per-release (e.g., stricter thresholds for LTS rollouts).

High-level checks included:
1) Lightweight smoke probes: endpoint connectivity, basic generation correctness for 5 canonical prompts, KV-loss detection.
2) Perf regression gate: compare latency P95 and token/sec to baseline with configurable thresholds (default: +10% latency, -8% throughput). Includes synthetic traffic that mirrors recent distribution.
3) Eval suite: targeted prompts and automated diffing against golden outputs for quality drift; supports multiple eval buckets (safety, hallucination, prompt-specific regressions).
4) LTS compatibility checks: model binary compatibility probe, quantization sanity, KV cache snapshot/restore validation.
5) Telemetry gates: error rate, signficant traces from tracing hooks, and anomaly detection signal (drift detector).

Proposed workflow:
- Release manager kicks off a PVG run as part of the rollout pipeline. PVG executes checks in parallel where possible, with weighted pass/fail aggregation.
- Failures produce an artifact bundle (logs, traces, failing evals) and automatically open a draft incident and a GitHub PR with revert suggestions if critical.
- If PVG passes, orchestration proceeds to the next stage. If it fails, rollout pauses and the on-call release engineer gets notified with triage steps.

Instrumentation and observability:
- Add per-check telemetry events and a summary health status that the Console can render as a stage card.
- Emit structured artifacts to S3/GCS with links in the ticket and console.

Rollout policy knobs (configurable):
- Thresholds per check, required pass rate, minimum canary duration, minimum sample size for perf gate, and forced manual approval flags for LTS.
- Ability to override with an enterprise override but must require 2 approvers and audit log entry.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Design and API for PVG plug-ins (2 wks) - define proto for checks and artifact schema.
2) Smoke + Perf gate prototype wired to synthetic harness and local runner (3 wks).
3) Eval-suite integration (3 wks) - support running multi-bucket evals and producing diffs.
4) LTS compatibility module (2 wks) - binary/quantization checks and KV snapshot tooling.
5) Console integration and alerting (2 wks).
6) GA rollout and docs (1 wk).

Trade-offs and open decisions:
- Strictness vs velocity: stricter thresholds delay rollouts but reduce incident risk. Default will be conservative for LTS, permissive for patch releases.
- Synthetic vs production shadow traffic: synthetic tests are faster and reproducible; shadowing is higher fidelity but riskier and more resource intensive. Plan to start with synthetic replay and add optional shadow lanes.
- Failure remediation automation: auto-revert on perf-critical failures vs pause-and-notify. Default to pause; consider auto-revert for P0 regressions after exec review.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Progressive+Validation+Gateway
- Synthetic workload repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/synthetic-replay/tree/pvg-prototype
- Draft runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/pvg-triage
- Related tickets: ENG-31207 (compatibility prober), ENG-39102 (staged-rollout safety validation)

Acceptance criteria (done):
- PVG can be executed end-to-end in staging and reports pass/fail for every gate with artifacts attached.
- Console stage card shows PVG status and links to artifacts.
- Team runbook updated and first 2 releases use PVG in pipeline.
